nodes.title: three-pinata runtime Voronoi fracture for Three.js
nodes.summary: Three.js library (v2.0.1) for runtime Voronoi (3D and 2.5D) fracture, impact-centred fracture, refracture and plane slicing with separate inner-face material.
nodes.why_it_matters: Most direct browser donor for mesh fracture; measured too slow for per-impact fracture of wall-sized slabs in The Alley M1, still a candidate for offline pre-fracture or small hero-chunk refracture.
caveats: Measured in Node 22 on a 4-core Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz cloud container (no GPU involvement): 2.5D exact fracture of a 6x4x0.35 m box took 62 ms for 30 fragments (3.7k tris), 182 ms for 60 impact-centred fragments (15.9k tris), 781 ms for 120 (56.7k tris), 2040 ms for 250 (89k tris); an 18x9 m facade at 600 fragments took 12.9 s and logged 'Failed to find final triangle'.
useApproximation=true cut 250 fragments to 145 ms / 21.9k tris but the library warns approximation may overlap fragments.
Refracturing one small fragment into ~12 pieces took 11-45 ms.
Browser timings not measured; Node timing excludes collider creation and GPU upload.

verification.method: npm package README/types read and library executed locally for timing; feature claims beyond the measured 2.5D box cases remain author-reported. Promote after pinning an upstream git commit.

outcomes.reason: Per-impact fracture latency (180-780 ms per panel) and triangle growth exceed the frame budget; The Alley pre-fractures infill into convex Voronoi prisms at load and removes cells at impact instead.

nodes.title: Pre-fractured convex Voronoi infill with cell removal (The Alley M1 lesson)
nodes.summary: Thick planar infill is tessellated at load into convex 2.5D Voronoi prisms (exact half-plane clipping, welded shared vertices); each prism is a Rapier convex-hull collider on one fixed body per panel. Impacts disable colliders and zero index ranges; removed cells become exact-shape hero rigid bodies or instanced cosmetic rubble; connectivity with weighted edge anchors releases unsupported clusters.
nodes.why_it_matters: Keeps visual holes, projectile collision and line of sight identical while keeping destruction ops in the low milliseconds; reusable for any browser destructible-cover project.
caveats: Measured only under headless Chromium 141 + SwiftShader on a 4-core Xeon 2.1 GHz: worst fixed simulation step 8.7-9.4 ms in salvo/ram/heavy scenarios after load-time warm-up (76 ms before warm-up); destruction ops 1-3 ms; reset 0.3-13 ms. GPU frame time on real hardware not measured.
Draw calls grow with persistent hero debris (323 pristine to ~1000 in a heavily damaged alley).
Hole outlines follow Voronoi cell edges at ~0.3-0.56 m scale; sub-cell irregularity is not modelled.
Fracture side faces need polygon offset or they z-fight with the outer face along every cell edge.

verification.method: Implemented and measured in-project (alley/tools/inspect.mjs; metrics in docs/alley/captures/metrics.json).
